leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part prize on B033 naming Daniel J. Drucker, Jens Juul Holst and Svetlana Mojsov, with citations centred on GLP-1 as an incretin hormone and identification of its active form. Shared: the physiology-centred framing, the exclusion of Lotte Bjerre Knudsen as industrial drug development, and the view that the discovery is mature and independently confirmed. Not shared or not settled: the wording of the citation (for example whether it should say 'first discovery' or only 'identification of the active peptide'), and the strength of confidence in Mojsov. Marie Wahren-Herlenius opened with Knudsen in place of Mojsov and in round 1 withdrew that substitution as the weaker choice, while still stating lower confidence in the exact trio than in the achievement itself. Agreement on the trio is explicit in the six files but is not the same as agreement that the attribution is resolved.

areas_of_agreement: B033 was placed first by all six members in the opening and is the explicit round-1 preferred configuration of all six, with the same three laureates.

The scientific case rests on a complete mechanistic chain (GLP-1 incretin physiology, identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, receptor biology) confirmed independently over decades and by large randomized outcome trials in glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints.

Maturity of B033 is not seen as a concern by any member; long-term safety and durability in obesity were raised only as an accumulating uncertainty, and Svenningsson-per stated that the evidence does not support waiting.

Members broadly agree that the prize should not depend on a company's development credit, and that Knudsen's contribution is real but is a different kind of contribution from the physiological discovery.

B036 (unfolded protein response; Mori and Walter) is described by several members as the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and is listed as an alternative by el-manira-abdel, perlmann-thomas, sandberg-rickard, svenningsson-per and wahren-herlenius-marie.

Members who discuss B011 (optogenetics) agree that its scientific value is exceptional but that six credited names against a three-person cap is a serious fairness obstacle, and none prefers it as a primary configuration.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus development for B033: whether the prize should reward physiology and peptide identification only, or also the medicinal chemistry behind liraglutide and semaglutide. All six prefer the physiology-only trio, but each lists this as an open uncertainty, and members acknowledge that excluding Knudsen may be read as a judgement against translation.

Weight of impact versus conceptual cleanliness: B036 is regarded as scientifically secure with mostly indirect or prospective medical consequences, whereas B033 combines a clear mechanism with demonstrated patient benefit. Members disagree on how much a tidy attribution should offset weaker established clinical effect.

B047 (SMN2 antisense) versus other alternatives: Linnarsson-sten values the direct mechanism-to-drug line and two-name credit, while other members view its discovery content as narrower and the field as younger.

B011 (optogenetics) as a tool-based discovery: it is accepted as having precedent for a methodological prize, but perlmann-thomas notes its value is as a research tool more than a physiology or disease finding, and clinical impact is still limited.

Whether still-accumulating long-term safety and durability data for GLP-1 agents in obesity should delay recognition; this was raised as a consideration by several members but not argued as a reason to wait.
attribution_disputes: Mojsov versus Habener (and colleagues, not on the credited list) over who first identified the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide. Every member states that this cannot be resolved from the supplied evidence. El-manira-abdel would fall back to Drucker and Holst only, not an industrial name, if the committee judges the evidence unresolved.

Third slot on B033: Mojsov versus Knudsen. Wahren-Herlenius's opening put Knudsen in place of Mojsov; the other five preferred Mojsov. Whether Knudsen should replace or accompany a basic scientist remains framed as a question about where discovery ends and industrial development begins.

B033 has four credited names (Drucker, Holst, Knudsen, Mojsov) plus uncredited early contributors competing for three places, so any trio is defensible to some and unfair to others. Perlmann-thomas and sandberg-rickard note that a second distinct prize part cannot be added without reducing B033 below three names.

B011: Nagel, Hegemann and Bamberg (channel side), Deisseroth and Boyden (neuronal deployment) and Miesenboeck (earlier photosensitization) are separable claims; el-manira-abdel's trio of Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann omits Bamberg and Boyden, and no principled line has been stated.

B013 (CAR-T): the credited trio of June, Sadelain and Rosenberg is questioned because Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer is a distinct earlier line and Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept is uncredited; several members regard June and Sadelain as the cleaner pair.

B036: mammalian PERK and ATF6 contributors are not credited, which perlmann-thomas notes could be raised as an omission. B043: attribution among Hall, Sabatini and Schreiber, with several groups converging on mTOR identification, is described as entangled; sandberg-rickard's Hall-only proposal is viewed by svenningsson-per as too narrow.
maturity_disputes: No member argues that B033 is premature. The only maturity-related reservation is whether long-term safety and durability data for newer agents are sufficiently complete; members who raise it do not think it justifies waiting.
B036: mechanism is thoroughly confirmed, but therapeutic modulation of the unfolded protein response has not yet produced a validated treatment, so medical maturity is contested relative to B033.
B047: the field of antisense therapy is described as younger, and Linnarsson-sten, perlmann-thomas and svenningsson-per variously regard it as better suited to a later year.
B011: the method is mature and transformative, but its clinical impact is still limited, so recognition rests on the tool rather than on disease outcomes.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson-per (chair) discloses roughly twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard; neither is a candidate and no credited shortlist name is documented as a collaborator, so no recusal is apparent.
Perlmann-thomas flags co-authored work with Per Svenningsson and one paper with Abdel El Manira, and does not regard it as grounds for recusal.

Sandberg-rickard discloses co-authorship with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen, not on any shortlisted candidate, and a topical interest in B047 through RNA splicing and single-cell methods, which is not his preferred candidate.
Wahren-Herlenius discloses a topical interest in immunology candidates such as B039 (cGAS-STING), which is not in her preferred configuration.

El-manira-abdel notes methodological familiarity with optogenetics (B011) and connections to Grillner, Ernfors and Perlmann, none involving a shortlisted candidate; linnarsson-sten lists co-authors (Betsholtz, Ernfors, Frisen, Castelo-Branco, Lundeberg, Kharchenko) not credited on any shortlisted ballot. No member reports a specific conflict with a credited name on the shortlist.
questions_for_round2: Does the primary literature support crediting Mojsov for identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide against the claim of Habener and colleagues, and if the committee cannot establish this, should the configuration fall back to Drucker and Holst only, to a different third name, or to another ballot?

Should the B033 citation be defined as physiology and identification of the active peptide only, and if so, what explicit wording avoids implying a first discovery of the incretin concept while acknowledging the therapies that followed?

Where does the committee draw the line between discovery and industrial development, and does that line exclude Knudsen under any citation, or is there a configuration in which she accompanies rather than replaces a basic scientist?
Is any second prize part feasible alongside B033 within the three-person limit, given that B033 requires three names, or should round 2 treat B033 as a single-part prize?

If B033 proves intractable on attribution, which alternative do members prefer as the fallback (B036 for clean attribution, B013 with a June and Sadelain pair, or another), and on what criteria of impact versus attribution cleanliness?

Can a defensible three-person cut be stated for B011 (a channelrhodopsin discovery plus neuronal-application split), or for B013 given Rosenberg's and Eshhar's roles, that most members would regard as fair? If not, should these ballots be set aside?
How much weight should long-term safety and durability data for GLP-1 agents in obesity carry in the timing judgement, and does any member now argue for deferral?
summary.chair_observation: The round-1 record shows unanimous explicit support for one configuration, B033 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, so the open work is not whether to recognise this discovery but whether the names and citation can be defended. Every member says the Mojsov versus Habener priority question cannot be settled from the supplied text, and every member excludes Knudsen on a discovery-versus-development rationale while acknowledging the cost. Alternatives are split in motivation: B036 is favoured for attribution clarity, B011 and B013 are favoured for impact but weakened by credit problems, and B047 is regarded as stronger for a later year. The counts above reflect only positions stated in the six files.
